term_definitions.items: Unique identifier for a CARE CONTACT
The unique identifier for a SERVICE REQUEST.
Unique local CARE PROFESSIONAL TEAM IDENTIFIER within a Health Care Provider and may be assigned automatically by the computer system.
The date, month, year and century, or any combination of these elements, that is of relevance to an ACTIVITY
The time (using a 24 hour clock) that is of relevance to an ACTIVITY.
ORGANISATION IDENTIFIER of the ORGANISATION commissioning health care.
NHS PATIENT, including Overseas Visitors charged under the National Health Service (Overseas Visitors Hospital Charging Regulations)
Private PATIENT, one who uses accommodation or SERVICES authorised under the National Health Service Act 2006
Amenity PATIENT, one who pays for the use of a single room or small ward in accordance with the National Health Service Act 2006

Category II PATIENT, one for whom work is undertaken by hospital medical or dental staff within category II as defined in paragraph 37 of the Terms and Conditions of Service of Hospital Medical and Dental Staff
Clinical Contact Duration of Care Contact

Total duration of the direct clinical contact at a CARE CONTACT in minutes, excluding any administration time prior to or after the CARE CONTACT and the CARE PROFESSIONAL's travelling time to the CARE CONTACT.
The type of consultation between the CARE PROFESSIONAL and the PATIENT.
The PERSON who was the subject of the CARE CONTACT.
The communication mechanism used to relay information between the CARE PROFESSIONAL and the PERSON who is the subject of the consultation, during a CARE CONTACT.
Talk type for a PERSON unable to speak
The type of LOCATION for an ACTIVITY.
Emergency Care Department or Minor Injuries Department
Integrated Care Home Services without Nursing and Care Home Services with Nursing
Street or other public open space
Other publicly accessible area or building
ORGANISATION SITE IDENTIFIER of the ORGANISATION SITE where the PATIENT was treated
An indication of whether a CARE ACTIVITY was delivered as Group Therapy
An indication of whether an APPOINTMENT for a CARE CONTACT took place
Attended on time or, if late, before the relevant CARE PROFESSIONAL was ready to see the PATIENT
Arrived late, after the relevant CARE PROFESSIONAL was ready to see the PATIENT, but was seen
PATIENT arrived late and could not be seen
APPOINTMENT cancelled by, or on behalf of, the PATIENT
Did not attend - no advance warning given
APPOINTMENT cancelled or postponed by the Health Care Provider

Patient Cancellations Where, for any reason, a PATIENT cancels or does not attend an APPOINTMENT or an OFFER OF ADMISSION the EARLIEST REASONABLE OFFER DATE for the rearranged APPOINTMENT or OFFER OF ADMISSION will be the EARLIEST REASONABLE OFFER DATE of the cancelled APPOINTMENT or OFFER OF ADMISSION
EARLIEST CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE DATE is the earliest date that it was clinically appropriate for an ACTIVITY to take place.
A Care Contact Cancellation Date is the date on which a CARE CONTACT was cancelled
A Replacement Appointment Date Offered is the replacement APPOINTMENT date offered to the PATIENT by the Health Care Provider following the cancellation of an APPOINTMENT
A Replacement Appointment Booked Date is the date on which a replacement APPOINTMENT was booked following the cancellation of an APPOINTMENT with the PATIENT by the Health Care Provider
A contact made with a PATIENT for the delivery of care.
A unique number or set of characters that is applicable to only one ACTIVITY for a PATIENT within an ORGANISATION.
A unique number or set of characters that is applicable to only one ACTIVITY for a PATIENT within an ORGANISATION.
The type of CARE ACTIVITY performed during a CARE CONTACT by a Community Health Service CARE PROFESSIONAL.
Health Visitor Formal handover to School Nursing Service (4-5 years)
A number or set of characters which uniquely identifies a CARE PROFESSIONAL.
Clinical Contact Duration of Care Activity

CLINICAL CONTACT DURATION OF CARE ACTIVITY is the total duration of a CARE ACTIVITY in minutes, excluding any administration time prior to or after the CARE ACTIVITY and the CARE PROFESSIONAL's travelling time to the LOCATION where the CARE ACTIVITY was provided.
The type of CODED CLINICAL ENTRY used for the CLINICAL INTERVENTION.
A unique clinical terminology identifier for a CODED CLINICAL ENTRY.
The type of CODED CLINICAL ENTRY used for the Finding.
The type of CLINICAL TERMINOLOGY CODE used for the observation.
The value of a CLINICAL INVESTIGATION RESULT ITEM.
The UNIT OF MEASUREMENT using the Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM) code system.
To carry details of any activities which have taken place as part of a contact with a patient. One occurrence of this group is permitted for each Care Activity.
Peak systemic arterial blood pressure - measured in systolic or contraction phase of the heart cycle.
Minimum systemic arterial blood pressure - measured in the diastolic or relaxation phase of the heart cycle.
Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.
The position of the individual at the time of measurement.
The size of the cuff used for blood pressure measurement.
Perloff D, Grim C, Flack J, Frohlich ED, Hill M, McDonald M, Morgenstern BZ. Human blood pressure determination by sphygmomanometry. Circulation 1993;88;2460-2470.
Simple body site where blood pressure was measured.
A cuff used for an adult thigh.
A cuff for adults with larger arms.
A cuff that is standard for an adult.
The right arm of the person.
The left arm of the person.
The right thigh of the person.
The left thigh of the person.
Additional narrative about the measurement, not captured in other fields.
Standing at the time of blood pressure measurement.
Sitting (for example on bed or chair) at the time of blood pressure measurement.
Reclining at the time of blood pressure measurement.
Lying flat at the time of blood pressure measurement.
The craniocaudal tilt of the surface on which the person is lying at the time of measurement.
The average arterial pressure that occurs over the entire course of the heart contraction and relaxation cycle.
The difference between the systolic and diastolic pressure.
A cuff used for a small adult.
A cuff that is appropriate for a child or adult with a thin arm.
Record which Korotkoff sound is used for determining diastolic pressure using auscultative method.
The fourth Korotkoff sound is identified as an abrupt muffling of sounds.
The fifth Korotkoff sound is identified by absence of sounds as the cuff pressure drops below the diastolic blood pressure.
Lying flat with some lateral tilt, usually angled towards the left side. Commonly required in the last trimester of pregnancy to relieve aortocaval compression.
A cuff used for a neonate, assuming cuff is the appropriate size for maturity and birthweight of the neonate.
The right wrist of the individual.
The left wrist of the individual.
Details about sphygmomanometer or other device used to measure the blood pressure.
The right ankle of the individual.
Details about physical activity undertaken at the time of blood pressure measurement.
The left ankle of the individual.
Method of measurement of blood pressure.
Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using a stethoscope and Korotkoff sounds.
Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using palpation (usually of the brachial or radial arteries).
Formula used to calculate the Mean Arterial Pressure (if recorded in data).
Method of measuring blood pressure externally, using a blood pressure machine.
Method of measuring blood pressure internally ie involving penetration of the skin and measuring inside blood vessels.
Estimate of the average blood pressure over a 24 hour period.
Sleep status - supports interpretation of 24 hour ambulatory blood pressure records.
The individual is in the natural state of bodily rest.

Comment on and record other incidental factors that may be contributing to the blood pressure measurement. For example, level of anxiety or 'white coat syndrome'; pain or fever; changes in atmospheric pressure etc.
Invasive measurement via transducer access line within an artery.
Formula used to calculate the systolic pressure from from mean arterial pressure (if recorded in data).
Formula used to calculate the diastolic pressure from mean arterial pressure (if recorded in data).
Structured anatomical location of where the measurement was taken.
Additional information required to capture local context or to align with other reference models/formalisms.
For example: Local hospital departmental infomation or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.
Single word, phrase or brief description that represents the clinical meaning and significance of the blood pressure measurement.
The individual's dorsum of the foot.
The local measurement of arterial blood pressure which is a surrogate for arterial pressure in the systemic circulation.
Most commonly, use of the term 'blood pressure' refers to measurement of brachial artery pressure in the upper arm.
A single, standard, OpenEHR OBSERVATION containing the data contained in the care activity metadata
One or more observations taking place during the care contact
